description: Pronunciation test cases for Hindi (Devanagari script)
notes: Hindi uses IPA notation. Key phonological rules tested: schwa deletion (both word-final and medial), geminate consonants, vowel length.

schwa_deletion.description: Hindi word-final and medial schwa deletion rules
schwa_deletion.notes: In Hindi, word-final schwas are typically deleted, and medial schwas are often deleted in certain contexts

geminate_consonants.notes: Geminate (doubled) consonants are phonemically distinct in Hindi

vowel_length.description: Testing long vs short vowel distinctions
vowel_length.notes: Hindi distinguishes between short and long vowels

nasal_assimilation.notes: Nasals assimilate to the place of articulation of following consonants

aspiration.notes: Hindi distinguishes between aspirated and unaspirated stops

test_cases.notes: Transliteration: kāma. Should produce /kaːm/ NOT /kaːmə/. The final schwa is deleted.
Transliteration: rāstā. Should produce /raːstaː/ NOT /raːsətaː/. Medial schwa before word-final syllable is deleted.
Transliteration: adṛśya. Contains initial schwa (typically present) and retroflex /ʂ/ from 'sh' conjunct.
Transliteration: kakṣā. Double 'k' creates geminates in the conjunct. Final schwa deleted.

test_cases.description: Consonant clusters with medial schwa deletion
test_cases.notes: Transliteration: patra. Shows schwa deletion before final /r/.
Transliteration: cala. Starts with palatal affricate /tʃ/.
Transliteration: nāma. Velar nasal /ŋ/ before word-final /m/.
Transliteration: kahānī. Long vowels marked with colon (:). Final /iː/ is long.
Transliteration: sundar. The anusvara (ं) creates /n/ before /d/.
Transliteration: yoga. Starts with palatal approximant /j/.
Transliteration: shahar. Begins with voiceless palatal fricative /ʃ/.
Transliteration: billī. Double 'l' creates geminate liquid. Final vowel is long.
Transliteration: dhanyavād. Initial /dʰ/ is aspirated. Includes schwa deletion.
Transliteration: aspatāl. Complex consonant cluster handling with schwa before /t/.
